Catalogue.x-meaning: The world source's own material vocabulary. emptyMaterialRef names the material that means an empty cell; it must be a key of materials.

EngineRevisions.x-meaning: Opaque revisions the world source reports for what defines its materials. Compared for equality only.

MaterialTags.x-meaning: Neutral tags the world source normalises from its own material definitions. placeable is the world source's conclusion that the material can be written and restored on its declared write path with no side effect and no persistent state; null is unknown and never treated as false or true. Raw engine fields stay in extension and are never read outside the world source.

OpaqueValue.x-meaning: Any strict JSON value owned by the world source. Carried and digested unchanged; never interpreted outside the world source.

Orientation.x-meaning: Neutral orientation index of a material, from the set the Catalogue declares for that material. Conversion to an engine encoding happens only inside the world source.

Ref.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path

RefV6.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path

Revision.x-normalization: NONE; opaque equality, never numeric ordering

World_AvatarEnvelope.x-meaning: The body envelope the world source declares for its player body: a fixed size it vouches for, the same for every player and every moment. Never a live position, yaw, posture or identity; players joining, leaving or moving never change it. UNAVAILABLE/NO_PUBLIC_SOURCE when the world source declares none; consumers then refuse by name, never fill a size.

World_AvatarSize.x-meaning: Extent in Frame grid units: width along x, height along the up axis, depth along z.

World_Catalogue.x-meaning: The world source's own material vocabulary. emptyMaterialRef names the material that means an empty cell; it must be a key of materials.

World_CatalogueFacts.x-meaning: The world source material vocabulary with names, colours and the neutral orientation index. presentation has exactly the Catalogue materials as keys; orientationIndex describes every orientation any material declares.

World_EngineFacts.x-meaning: Geometry, partition, bounds, frame, lighting and write facts the world source declares for the paired connection. engineBounds null means the world source declares no bound.

World_EngineFrame.x-meaning: The world source coordinate frame: axis directions, handedness and grid unit. A Frame for one target adds origin and revision.

World_EngineRevisions.x-meaning: Opaque revisions the world source reports for what defines its materials. Compared for equality only.

World_MaterialPresentation.x-meaning: How the world source names and colours one material for people and for image material matching. null is unknown, never a default name or colour.

World_MaterialSourceFacts.x-meaning: Material sources and colours for image material selection. presentation has exactly the materialRefs of snapshot.materials as keys. Texture bytes are not on the wire: they are referenced by bytesDigest and travel through the in-process material sources port.

World_MaterialTags.x-meaning: Neutral tags the world source normalises from its own material definitions. placeable is the world source's conclusion that the material can be written and restored on its declared write path with no side effect and no persistent state; null is unknown and never treated as false or true. Raw engine fields stay in extension and are never read outside the world source.

World_OpaqueValue.x-meaning: Any strict JSON value owned by the world source. Carried and digested unchanged; never interpreted outside the world source.

World_Orientation.x-meaning: Neutral orientation index of a material, from the set the Catalogue declares for that material. Conversion to an engine encoding happens only inside the world source.

World_OrientationDescriptor.x-meaning: Neutral meaning of one orientation index: clockwise quarter turns about the Frame up axis seen from above, and whether the material is flipped upside down. null means the world source has no neutral expression for that part; the conversion to an engine encoding stays inside the world source.

World_Partition.x-meaning: The world source's storage partition of a voxel-grid world: cells are grouped into boxes of edge[x,y,z] cells aligned at multiples of edge on each axis. Region payloads are cut along it. Declared by the world source; never assumed.

World_PostWriteLighting.x-meaning: REQUIRED: after a region write the world source recalculates light for the written box and reports a RegionLighting fact; a VERIFIED region commit or undo needs it COMPLETE. NONE: the world source has no separate light pass; no lighting fact exists and none is checked.

World_Ref.x-normalization: NONE; exact Unicode scalar sequence; never trim/lower/NFC; not a path

World_Revision.x-normalization: NONE; opaque equality, never numeric ordering

World_SrgbColor.x-meaning: An sRGB colour as lower-case #rrggbb. The world source decides how it is obtained (declared, or from its own assets); consumers compare and match colours only.

World_WorldGeometry.x-meaning: What the world source declares about its geometry. geometryProfiles is open: it may name profiles this contracts major does not define, and a payload profile absent from it is a CAPABILITY_GAP. partition is non-null exactly when voxel-grid/v1 is declared.

World_WriteBackendRef.x-meaning: Opaque identity of the world source's write backend. Compared for equality only.

World_WriteMethods.x-meaning: The write methods the world source supports on the paired connection. A method not listed is not supported; nothing is implied by a package or wire version.

World_WriteProfile.x-meaning: Everything a host needs to forward for writing: opaque write backend, the complete compilation configuration, supported write methods and the body envelope. compilationConfig is non-null exactly when writeBackend is KNOWN and then carries that writeBackend unchanged. A host forwards it as is: it never interprets, completes or defaults a field.
